name: The State Hermitage Museum
notes: The Hermitage on the Palace Embankment, the whole ensemble at a coarse voxel, from its published plans and descriptions; no photographs were available. Set to the embankment, which runs 57 degrees east of north here (read off the ground file). Rastrelli's Winter Palace (1754-62): four ranges of pale green and white round the Great Courtyard, white columns in tiers round every front, the balustrade with its statues and urns, the roofs, the three arches of the gate on Palace Square; the Small Hermitage and its hanging garden, the yellow Old Hermitage beside it along the river, Klenze's New Hermitage behind on Millionnaya Street with the granite Atlantes' porch, the Winter Canal and the Hermitage Theatre across it; the Neva and its granite quay; the Alexander Column on Palace Square. Guessed: the ranges' depths, all heights (22 m to the cornice), the column spacing, the building colours other than the Winter Palace's; the General Staff Building's arc across the square is off the plate.
